title: Putting Back Overdraft Charges Taken Above the Personal Checking Fee Schedule
content:
Where the overdraft charges standing on a Personal Checking account are larger than the charges the published fee schedule produces for the same run of items, the bank puts the difference back as one corrective entry on the bank-error ground, recorded against the largest of the overdraft charges under review. The owner keeps the original overdraft charges on the record and sees the corrective credit beside them, and the account's posted ledger balance rises by the corrected amount.

An account carrying no overdraft charge above the schedule is outside this rule and no corrective entry is made.

## Recording the entry

The corrective entry is booked with the tool `post_fee_schedule_correction_961f83a2`, which the agent unlocks and then calls. It books a single correction entry credited to the named checking account, marked as a bank error and tied to the overdraft charge it corrects. Nothing else on the account changes.

### Parameters

| Parameter | What it is | Form |
|---|---|---|
| `checking_account_id` | The reference number of the Personal Checking account the correction is credited to, taken from the checking account lookup for this owner | Reference number |
| `customer_id` | The reference number of the customer profile that owns the account, as returned by the customer profile lookup; it is stamped on the entry so the owner's refund record stays complete | Reference number |
| `source_item_id` | The reference number of the single overdraft charge entry on the account that is being corrected, read from the account's posted activity | Reference number |
| `correction_amount` | The money credited back, in United States dollars to 2 decimal places, always positive and rounded half-up to the cent at the moment of the call; there is no empty value and zero is not accepted | Fixed format |
| `statement_cycle` | The statement cycle the entry belongs to, written as the year and month in which that cycle closes, with no day part and no time zone | Fixed format |

### Return

The call answers with a confirmation sentence carrying the reference number minted for the new correction entry, the corrected amount to the cent, and the account's posted ledger balance after the credit. That sentence naming a correction entry reference number is what shows the call completed; the credit is then visible in the account's posted activity.
